teardown.label: Real-world proof · Teardown #001
teardown.title: We ran Olmene on Olmene.
teardown.body: Before telling you what to fix, we pointed our own tool at our own homepage. It found five issues and scored us 89/100 — not a perfect score, because it doesn't know it's measuring us. We fixed everything it found the same day:
teardown.li1: Meta description trimmed from 181 to 155 characters
teardown.li2: Canonical URL added to every page
teardown.li5: This very section — its screenshot gives our image-alt check something to check
teardown.lesson: One finding taught us the most: after adding the JSON-LD, the check still failed — our own parser couldn't read @graph markup, the format most modern sites emit. So we fixed the instrument itself, redeployed, and re-measured. Every number on this page is real output, not a mockup.
teardown.afterLi1: All flagged issues fixed and re-measured
teardown.afterLi2: Re-run any time — the checks never soften
teardown.screenshotAlt: Olmene's free diagnosis card re-run on the Olmene homepage after the fixes: 98/100 marketing readiness, 18 of 18 checks passed, with the methodology disclosure listing every check
teardown.figcaption: Re-run after the fixes: 98/100 readiness, 18/18 checks — actual output on olmene.com, the same instrument you get.
teardown.quotesLabel: What our own full report added on top
teardown.q1: No JSON-LD structured data — missing Product, Price, FAQPage, and Review markup for rich results.
teardown.q1note: — flagged, then fixed the same day (see above).
teardown.q2: Trust signals (review/rated) are detected but no visible testimonials, logos, or case studies appear on the homepage.

faq.label: Questions
faq.title: Frequently asked, honestly answered.
faq.q1: Is this just ChatGPT with extra steps?
faq.a1: No. ChatGPT brainstorming starts from nothing and can't verify your website. Every Olmene report runs live web research on your market, reads your competitors' actual sites, and computes technical checks from your real HTML — then cites every market claim so you can check the reasoning yourself. Generic AI chat is useful for drafting; this is a structured, repeatable analysis.
faq.q2: How do I know the research is accurate?
faq.a2: Three ways. Market claims carry numbered citations you can open. Competitors are verified — we fetch their real websites instead of trusting a model's memory. And the 18-point SEO checklist is deterministic: it's computed from your HTML, not generated. You still get an AI-generated report, so we encourage verifying facts before acting — that's why the sources are in there.
faq.q3: How long does a report take?
faq.a3: Usually three to ten minutes. The analysis runs as ten verifiable steps — you can watch the progress live, and if you close the tab the report still finishes and waits on your dashboard.
faq.q4: What happens after my first report?
faq.a4: You work the plan: quick wins this week, then the 30/60/90-day actions. When you've shipped changes, run the analysis again — your scores update, so you can see whether the messaging, conversion and SEO work actually moved the needle, and what to fix next.
faq.q5: Why a subscription instead of a one-off report?
faq.a5: Because marketing isn't one-off. Your competitors change, your site changes, your positioning should too. Plans are sized for a realistic cadence — regular strategic reviews on Starter, continuous iteration on Pro. Cancel anytime; you keep access until the period ends.
faq.q6: What if my website is very small — or pre-launch?
faq.a6: Small is fine: the audit checks what's there and the strategy tells you what to add first. Fully pre-launch (no public site yet) doesn't work yet — the analysis is built around your live pages. Come back when the landing page is up.
faq.a7: Yes — one click in the customer portal. You keep access until the end of the period you paid for, and reports you already generated stay in your account forever. Failed analyses never count against your quota.

lp.s1.p: {{Account data:}} your email address (for magic-link sign-in) and a user ID. {{Analysis data:}} the URL you submit, the optional context you add (product name, market, competitors, goal), the reports we generate for you, and technical job metadata. {{Usage data:}} aggregate, non-identifying metrics like feature usage counts.
lp.s2.p: No passwords (magic links only), no payment card data (handled entirely by Polar, our merchant of record), no third-party ad trackers, and no analytics cookies unless you accept them in the cookie banner.
lp.s3.p: Account and analysis data exist to provide the service: run your analyses, store your reports, and enforce your plan quota. We don't sell your data, and we don't use your report content to train models.
lp.s4.p: When you submit a URL, our crawler fetches that site's public pages — like a search engine would. We identify ourselves with a descriptive user agent and respect standard technical limits (timeout, page-size caps, few pages per site).
lp.s5.p: Your reports stay in your account for as long as it exists. If you delete your account, we delete your reports, jobs and account data within 30 days, except where retention is legally required.
lp.s6.p: You can request a copy or deletion of your personal data at any time (GDPR/EU residents: this is your Art. 15/17 right). Contact us and we will comply within 30 days.
lp.s7.p: We use Google Analytics 4 — but only after you click {{Accept}} in the cookie banner. It shows once, the first time you visit, and you can accept or reject it. If you accept, Google sets {{_ga}} cookies to distinguish anonymous visitors (no personal profiles, and Google Analytics reports never include your IP address). If you reject, no Google Analytics code loads at all. You can change your choice anytime via {{Cookie preferences}} in the footer — rejecting again deletes the analytics cookies. Your Accept/Reject choice itself is stored in your browser's local storage, not on our servers.
lp.s8.p: Olmene relies on: Supabase (accounts, database, edge compute), Polar (payments, merchant of record), and AI/research providers (report generation, live web research). All process data only on our instructions.
lt.s1.p: Olmene (“we”) provides AI-generated marketing analysis reports based on public web data and the website URL you submit. Reports are research aids, not professional consulting advice. You are responsible for verifying facts and figures before acting on them.
lt.s2.p: You need an account to run analyses. You are responsible for activity under your account and for providing a website URL you have the right to have analyzed. Don't use the service to crawl or probe sites you don't control with malicious intent.
lt.s3.p: Paid plans renew monthly until cancelled. Payments, taxes and invoices are handled by Polar (merchant of record). You can cancel any time — access continues until the end of the paid period. Failed analyses never count against your quota. Refunds for the current period are handled on a case-by-case basis; contact support.
lt.s4.p: Don't resell reports as your own consulting work without disclosure, don't attempt to overload the service, and don't use reports to make legal, financial or investment decisions.
lt.s5.p: Reports are generated by AI systems from public web data and may contain inaccuracies. Market estimates carry confidence levels and citations; technical checks are deterministic. We combine both, but ultimate judgment stays with you.
lt.s6.p: The service is provided {{as is.}} To the maximum extent permitted by law, our liability is limited to the amount you paid in the three months preceding a claim.
lt.s7.p: We may update these terms; material changes will be announced in-app. Continued use after changes take effect means acceptance.
